title: Software
description: What runs code over a software map: the handoff, the release gate, proof on each build, rechecks and the changelog. Its words are the code pack's, its proof the proof pack's.

types.title: Diagram
types.description: One page of a diagram made from the code (npm run diagrams), kept as data its page draws: boxes, areas and the wires between them, at the commit it was made from.

diagram.description: The page as data: its boxes with where each is, its wires, the draw.io file and page it is (key), the commit it was drawn from, and that file at the commit (drawio) when it was committed as drawn.

rules.say: This reply made commits the map does not account for. In one change: a commit (full sha) each, a settles link per item it settles, or none; one heard from a push: accounted true.

views.description: Where a repository's work stands, for the session picking it up: the last push, what has happened in the last week (pushes, what was settled, what was opened, the sessions that ended and what each said: how many of each, and the newest five), the open work, ready and blocked, what ended sessions left on no remote or not committed (left), what nobody has seen working (unseen) and the traps in its files (traps). Read this first. Params: repo (required): its id, GitHub name or title; since (an ISO date-time to count from, instead of a week back).

repo.description: The repository: its id, its GitHub name "owner/name", or its title.

since.description: An ISO date-time to count from, instead of a week back.

full.description: true for the answer whole, as the screen has it.

views.description: An event as a gate (a release, a launch): what it waits for (everything it depends_on), grouped by stream (the feature or project each is part of) with progress and what the owner owes; what it goes ahead without (what it defers); what is not yet sorted (open tasks, issues and decisions under what it ships, on neither side); and how we know (the proof questions of what it ships and of what holds it, answered or not on the release’s build: its version). Params: event (an item id; without it, the open events that have a gate).

event.description: The event: an item id. Without it, the open events that have a gate.

full.description: true for the answer whole, as the screen has it.

views.description: Open tasks, decisions and issues belonging to whatever lives in a repository, split into ready and blocked, and when GitHub last reported a push to it. Params: repo (required): its id, its GitHub name "owner/name", or its title.

repo.description: The repository: its id, its GitHub name "owner/name", or its title.

full.description: true for the answer whole, as the screen has it.

views.description: What is due for a scheduled re-check in a repository: each project living there says how often its oldest items are re-checked (its recheck_days; weekly when not set, 0 for never; a feature living there on its own takes its project's), and for each that has waited that long (waited), its open items nobody has changed or confirmed in that time, oldest first, leaving out what waits on a person. Params: repo (required): its id, GitHub name or title, limit (items per project, default 25), now (true to be given the oldest items of every project there, whatever its interval and however new they are).

repo.description: The repository: its id, its GitHub name "owner/name", or its title.

now.description: true for the oldest items of every project there, whatever its interval.

views.description: How we know the software is correct: the proof questions of a product (a project or feature; a question is a proof that is part of it or about it), each with the tests that help answer it and what every test found on one build, with its picture. A question is answered on a build when all its tests passed there. Params: of (an entity id; without it, the projects that have proof questions), build (a version or commit; without it, the build last reported).

of.description: A project or feature; without it, the projects that have proof questions.

build.description: A version or commit; without it, the build last reported.

within.description: In place of of: only these items and what is part of them (a gate's stake, a public page's items).

full.description: true for the answer whole, as the screen has it.

views.description: What a product has to show: its features that are built or shipped, each with the release it went out in; built and not yet released first, then the newest. Planned work is not in it. Params: of (required): a project or feature.

within.description: Only these items, as a public page gives them.

full.description: true for the answer whole, as the screen has it.

views.title: Roadmap
views.description: A project's features in the order they are to be built, the work under each, and where work is happening now.

actions.title: Report a test run
actions.description: Say what a test run found on one build. Each result names its test by id or by its entrypoint (the name the harness knows it by) and says whether it passed, with the measured value, where the evidence is and the picture the test drew. One result is kept per test per build: reported again, it is replaced, and the pictures kept for that test's results are removed. Where a test answers a public question, the answer names the pictures to send now (answer.send_pictures: each with picture_put). A test the map does not know is named in the answer (answer.unknown) and nothing is made for it: create the test first and link it to the proof question it helps answer. Called as test_report.

build.description: The version or commit the tests ran on.

test.description: The test: its id, or its entrypoint.

value.description: The headline number or outcome, e.g. "0.004 degrees".

evidence.description: Where the proof is: a path, URL or commit.

picture.description: Where the picture the test drew is: a path in the repository, under its .proof folder (which git ignores), e.g. ".proof/1.0.0/Sun.MatchesNoaa.png". The file is not sent here.

link.description: Where the run can be looked at.

styles.title: Lay out the build and agree it first
styles.body: Before your first edit to a file, lay the build out on the map as items, part_of the task you work on, and have the owner agree it. Each part (type part) explains its code above all: which file and lines it covers, what they do and why they are written that way. Beside the parts: each file it makes or changes (type file), the tests that show it works (type test), the risks (type issue), and small steps, each with props.tokens_estimated and ordered by depends_on, so the task's estimate is their sum; a step too large to estimate well is broken into parts. The task's note holds only why and what done is, never the build as prose. Give the task a flow view of its steps (a lens linked about it, its style shape flow). Then link the task waits_on the owner (props.for: agree the build), show that view with report, action show, and write code once they have agreed and the link is removed.

styles.title: Build a drawing as a layout on the map
styles.body: When the work is a drawing, a diagram or any view that paints (three.js included), build it on the map, not as a local sketch or page: a layout item whose code draws it, drawn by a view (a lens whose style names it), shown to the owner with report, action show, so they watch it on their canvas as it grows. Code an agent writes waits for the owner before it runs. How a layout's code is written: query with name instructions, params for guide:style_code.

styles.title: How a layout's code is written
styles.body:
A layout item's `code` is one JavaScript module that draws a view. It runs in the browser of whoever looks, in a worker inside a sandboxed frame: no page, no network, no storage, no imports.

## Its function
`export default function draw({ canvas, answer, style, theme, size, tree, three, on, open, tip, cursor, field, change })`
- `canvas`: an OffscreenCanvas to paint, 2D or WebGL; `size` is { width, height, dpr }, kept current, and on('resize') hears it change.
- `answer`: what the view's query answered (items and links); `tree()` gives it as a tree ({ root, byId, me }); on('answer') hears it again as the map changes (code that does not listen is started again).
- `style`: what it is drawn with (the layout's `settings`, under the style and the view's own), so every number the owner may change is a setting, never a constant; `theme`: the page's colours and whether it is dark.
- `three()`: resolves to three.js, for a WebGL scene on the canvas.

## Events and acts
- on(name, fn) hears pointerdown, pointermove, pointerup, pointerleave and wheel ({ x, y, button, buttons, deltaY, shift, ctrl }).
- open(id) opens an item's page; tip(text, x, y) shows words by the pointer (null hides them); cursor(name) sets the pointer.
- field(key, { x, y, width, height, value, placeholder, title }) has the page draw a text field; on('field') hears { key, value, done }.
- change(ops, reason) asks the page to send ops as the person looking: it applies where it writes only the types in the layout's `writes`, and waits for that person otherwise.

## Making one
- create a layout with props.code (and props.settings for its numbers), and a lens about the work with props.style { style: {ref} } and the query it draws; show it with report, action show.
- The code waits for the owner each time you change it; say what changed in the reason.
- query with name look sees it as the owner does.
